# Compositions: Narrative Family

Pages that explain or persuade in sequence. These include page shapes adapted from the Hallmark
project (long document, stat-led, workbench, split narrative, sticky feature stack, map/diagram,
index-first), rewritten around content requirements and failure conditions.

The rule that matters most: **choose by what the content can support.** A stat-led page needs a real
number; a workbench tour needs a real product; a long document needs a real argument.

---

## Editorial spread

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | A story with visual rhythm |
| Content needs | Headline, deck, body, images with captions, pull quotes |
| Hierarchy / focal | Headline and lead image; then reading rhythm |
| Responsive | Collapse to a single reading column; keep image order meaningful |
| Fails when | Prose is broken into cards |
| Precedent | The Guardian (GU3), The Pudding (PU2) |

## Long document

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | An argument or explanation read top to bottom (memos, manifestos, changelogs, essays) |
| Content needs | A real argument; section heads that tell the story alone |
| Hierarchy / focal | Title and opening paragraph |
| Viewport | Text starts in the first viewport |
| Fails when | There is nothing to argue; it becomes filler prose |

## Full-bleed narrative

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | Image-led storytelling in chapters |
| Content needs | Strong, consistent imagery per chapter; one idea per chapter |
| Hierarchy / focal | Each chapter's image and one line |
| Scroll | Chapter by chapter; no scroll-jacking |
| Accessibility | Text alternatives; reduced motion |
| Fails when | The first viewport has no statement of what this is (XB1) |
| Precedent | Apple (AP2, AP3), Xbox (XB1) as a warning |

## Stat-led

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | One number is the message |
| Content needs | A real, specific, current number and its context |
| Hierarchy / focal | The number, then what it means |
| Fails when | The number is vanity or invented |
| Precedent | Stripe live figure (SR2), Cloudflare "20% of the Internet" (CF1) |

## Workbench tour

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | Explaining a tool by showing it in use |
| Content needs | Real, legible screenshots or embedded demos of actual tasks |
| Hierarchy / focal | The product in use; copy explains what the user does |
| Responsive | Screenshots must stay legible or switch to cropped details on phones |
| Fails when | Screenshots are fake, tilted into illegibility, or show empty states |
| Precedent | Cursor (CU1), Slack (SL2) |

## Split narrative

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | Claims paired with proof, alternating sides |
| Content needs | Each claim has specific proof (screenshot, number, quote) |
| RTL | Mirror the alternation |
| Fails when | Proof is decorative art |

## Sticky feature stack

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | Several related features explained in sequence |
| Content needs | 3–6 features with real visuals |
| Scroll | A sticky label pane beside scrolling visuals; must work without sticky on small screens |
| Accessibility | Keyboard and screen reader order must match |
| Fails when | Sticky behavior traps or confuses scroll |

## Map / diagram

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | A system understood spatially (architecture, process, ecosystem) |
| Content needs | A diagram that explains faster than text |
| Accessibility | A text description or list equivalent |
| Fails when | Used as decoration or in place of a narrative that is not spatial |

## Index-first

| Aspect | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Solves | The page is a list of destinations |
| Content needs | Many real destinations with clear labels |
| Precedent | Hacker News (HN1), Linear Docs "Popular" (LD2), Wikipedia structure |
| Fails when | Destinations are few; a list looks abandoned |
